protocol: Two fresh blind @vision reads per repo on the 1440x900 final frame; one image per task; no source, no sibling views, no expected answer; describe-first then strict JSON {question_answered, action, blockers, confidence}. The image self-identifies as MAP CANDIDATE G; the reads are blind to the other candidate and to the source.
animation: CSS/SMIL declarative only; final frame captured with prefers-reduced-motion; the artifact contains no JavaScript.

cJSON.description: This is a Perfpal "MAP CANDIDATE G · ENTRY-FLOW" view titled "cJSON — estimated static flow", answering which symbol is the entry when a library has no production `main` (header: "ENTRY · library root (no production main)", chosen entry "cJSON.c:253 · cJSON_Delete", confidence MEDIUM, with 2 alternatives listed at cJSON.c:2609 and cJSON.c:1227). The main canvas is a depth-0 flow diagram: one orange-highlighted ENTRY node ("cJSON.c — 2,905 static cost units (v2) — 3.30× median function") fans out via amber edges to five grey, dashed-outline nodes — cJSON_Utils.c, fuzzing/afl.c, test.c, fuzzing/cjson_read_fuzzer.c, fuzzing/fuzz_main.c — each labelled with static cost units, a "× median function" multiple, and "unreached", with an edge label of 56 distinct calls and looping dashed amber back-edges on their right sides. The right rail shows six "FILE CARDS" repeating those per-file stats plus top functions (e.g. cJSON.c: cJSON_Delete top 1%, print_object top 1%) and codes such as "PERF-C-STR-003 · 11× · warn" and "PERF-C-ARCH-003 · 5× · info". The status line reads "6 files shown · 1 reachable (entry) · 0 reachable aggregated · 5 unreached production (grey)" and the canvas right corner says "UNREACHED — no forward path", so nothing beyond depth 0 is traversable. What stands out: the entry file is huge and warned (2,905 cost units, 3.30× median → 118 ms) while every neighbour is stranded, and the one card with a 52.0× median multiple (cJSON_Utils.c) is itself unreachable.

json.question_answered: ENTRY · library root (no production main): which symbol is the entry (highest fan-in production lib-root, no production main), and what does it flow to at depth 0?
json.action: Open cJSON.c and inspect cJSON_Delete at line 253 (the chosen entry) and compare it against the two listed alternatives cJSON.c:2609 and cJSON.c:1227 to confirm the entry pick.
json.blockers: All 5 outgoing neighbours are grey 'unreached — no forward path', so the flow stops at depth 0 and no downstream path can be traced; edge label numbers on the canvas (e.g. 56) are small and edges are declared 'structural and LOW confidence'.

The header names the entry in red as "ENTRY · library root (no production main)" — specifically `cJSON.c:253 · cJSON_Delete`, described as the "highest fan-in production lib-root," with confidence MEDIUM and two alternatives (`cJSON.c:2609`, `cJSON.c:1227`). The main canvas has one dark, orange-outlined node at "DEPTH 0 · ENTRY" (`cJSON.c`, 2,805 static cost units (v2), 3.503× median function) and five grey "unreachable" file nodes to its right (cJSON_Utils.c, fuzzing/afl.c, test.c, fuzzing/cjson_read_fuzzer.c, fuzzing/fuzz_main.c), each showing static cost units and a multiple of the repo-wide median function cost (e.g. fuzzing/afl.c at 40.5×). Curved dashed-amber back-edges fan out from the entry to those five nodes with an edge label of "56" (distinct call count), and the top-right region is marked "UNREACHED · no forward path," meaning nothing is reachable forward past depth 0 — the summary line confirms "6 files shown · 1 reachable (entry) · 0 reachable aggregated · 5 unreached production (grey)." json.action: Inspect cJSON.c:253 (cJSON_Delete), the selected ENTRY, and check why its forward path is empty (all 5 other files unreachable) — or evaluate the stated alternatives cJSON.c:2609 and cJSON.c:1227 as entry candidates

hyperfine.description: This is a single-screen dashboard titled "PERFPAL · MAP CANDIDATE G · ENTRY-FLOW" showing the "hyperfine" project's "estimated static flow," anchored at "ENTRY · production main — src/main.rs:88 · main" with "confidence HIGH." The main canvas is a left-to-right layered graph (DEPTH 0 · ENTRY through DEPTH 4) where each rounded box is a source file labeled with its name, "static cost units (v2)," and a "median function" millisecond figure; `src/main.rs` is the dark ENTRY node, and `src/command.rs` is flagged "HOTTEST" with an amber border (611 static cost units, 87.4 ms median). Curved orange/red lines are the "path trace" out of the entry, amber dashed lines are "back-edges," and a header line reports "19 of 19 reachable files shown... all 49 shown file pairs drawn (26 back-edges)" plus a note that "call edges are structural and LOW confidence." A footer box notes "~21 unreachable production files · no forward path." The right rail, "FILE CARDS · 19 shown · top functions by function_cost_v2," lists each file's category (production/test/bench), cost units, median time, its top functions with percentage shares (e.g. `src/command.rs`: "build - top 4%", "build_from_cli_arguments - top 2%"), and finding tags such as "PERF-RS-ARCH-003 ×22 · info" or "PERF-RS-ARCH-001 ×5 · warn." Top-right controls read "Q2 reverse drill · src/quantity/mod.rs →" and "Pause animation (CSS)." What stands out is that cost and time concentrate in `src/command.rs`, `src/metric.rs`, and `src/options.rs` on the entry path, while several small files show "no findings."

json.question_answered: ENTRY-FLOW: what is the estimated static flow out of the production main entry (src/main.rs:88 · main), and which files carry the most static cost along that path?
json.action: Profile src/command.rs::build — the HOTTEST node on the entry path (611 static cost units (v2), 87.4 ms median function, 'build - top 4%' in its file card, PERF-RS-ARCH-003 ×22).

hyperfine.description: This is a static-analysis map titled "PERFPAL · MAP CANDIDATE G · ENTRY-FLOW" showing "hyperfine estimated static flow": how cost flows outward from the program's entry point, `src/main.rs:88 · main` (labelled "ENTRY · production main", confidence HIGH). The main canvas is a left-to-right layered graph across columns DEPTH 0 (ENTRY) → DEPTH 1…4, where each rounded card is a source file showing its name, "static cost units (v2)," and "µs median function" — e.g. `src/main.rs` (58 units, 8.3µs) feeds depth-1 files `src/command.rs` (611 units, 82.4µs, flagged HOTTEST), `src/options.rs`, `src/shell_syntax.rs`, `src/benchmark/scheduler.rs`, and `src/cli.rs`, which in turn feed depth-2 files like `src/metric.rs` (431 units) and `tests/execution_order_tests.rs` (373 units). Gray arrows are forward caller→callee edges, dashed amber/red edges are back-edges (26 of the 49 drawn pairs), and an orange traced path highlights the entry → `src/command.rs` → `src/metric.rs` spine; a note says "+21 unreachable production files · no forward path". The header strip summarizes coverage: "19 of 19 reachable files shown", edges are "structural and LOW confidence", and the entry policy excludes build scripts, tests, and fuzzing. The right panel lists 19 "FILE CARDS · top functions by function_cost_v2", each card giving the file's kind, cost, slowest functions with their share (e.g. `src/command.rs`: `spawn` – top 40%), and related findings such as "PERF-RS-ARCH-003 x22 · info" or "PERF-RS-ARCH-001 x5 · warn" (`src/export/mod.rs`), with some files marked "no findings". Controls at top-right offer a "Q2 reverse drill · src/quantity/mod.rs →" and "Pause animation (CSS)".

json.question_answered: ENTRY-FLOW: from the production main entry (src/main.rs:88 · main), what is hyperfine's estimated static flow — which reachable files inherit cost, how deep they sit, and which are hottest?
json.action: Profile the hottest spine: src/command.rs function `spawn` (top 40% of its 611 static cost units, 82.4µs median — the HOTTEST node on the entry path), starting from src/main.rs:88

tmux.description: This is a single-screen dashboard titled "PERFPAL · MAP CANDIDATE G · ENTRY-FLOW" showing "tmux — estimated static flow," anchored at an ENTRY badge reading "ENTRY · production main / tmux.c:434 · main" with "confidence HIGH · alternatives: 0," plus buttons "Q2 reverse drill · tmux.h →" and "Pause animation (CSS)." The main canvas is a left-to-right call-flow graph banded into columns DEPTH 0 · ENTRY through DEPTH 5, where each rectangular node is a source file card showing its filename, "static cost units (v2)," and "median function" cost (e.g., depth-0 dark node tmux.c: 758 static cost units, 92.9µs median function). Curved amber edges connect callers to callees (footer: "forward callers → callees only · grey = unreached · dashed amber = back-edge"), and one depth-2 node, format.c (6,030 static cost units, 332µs median), is flagged "HOTTEST." A stats strip reads "20 of 106 reachable files shown: 86 unreachable files aggregated · 99 unreached production (counted, not drawn) · edges: 57 of 145 shown file pairs drawn (top by call count, 49 back-edges) · call edges are structural and LOW confidence." Deeper levels collapse into placeholders like "+39 more / depth 3 · 330 calls in," and the bottom-left notes "...+99 unreached production files · no forward path." The right rail, "FILE CARDS · 20 shown · top functions by function_cost_v2 · top finding rule," lists each file with its top functions (e.g., format.c → format_replace - top 1%, format_expand1 - top 1%) and a rule tag such as "PERF-C-ARCH-003 <399 · info." What stands out: flow from main fans out heavily at depth 2 into format.c/window.c/tty.c, and the biggest cost concentration sits in format.c and window-copy.c (5,100 units).

json.question_answered: ENTRY-FLOW — from the production entry tmux.c:434 · main, how does estimated static flow (function_cost_v2) distribute across the codebase?
json.action: Drill into tmux.c:434 (main) and profile format.c's format_replace (top 1% of format.c's 6,030 static cost units, marked HOTTEST at depth 2), the heaviest node on the entry path.
json.blockers: Call edges are explicitly labelled structural and LOW confidence; depths 4-5 are collapsed into '+7 more' / '+1 more' placeholders so deeper flow is not inspectable.

json.action: Drill into the HOTTEST node format.c (6,030 static cost units, 332.+ median function) starting with its top function format_expand1 (top 1%), and run the "Q2 reverse drill - tmux.h →" button to trace callers back toward tmux.c:434 main

verdict: G: 6/6 valid reads state the entry question and one concrete file/function action. Hyperfine and tmux read strongly (entry + HOTTEST + action); cJSON is an honest structural dead-end (library, no production main, one reachable node) and both reads report the missing forward path. Units/anchors are present after the fix; function names are full; edge labels are explained.
observations: O1: cJSON is the library case — G answers 'what is the entry' but not 'how does the program flow'; the forward graph is empty and the 5 production callers are greyed. This is a data-shape limitation, not a layout bug.
O2: hyperfine and tmux produce the intended story: entry -> hottest file (src/command.rs; format.c) -> action. The path trace and depth rings are read correctly.
O3: hyperfine's two reads chose different top functions inside src/command.rs (build vs spawn) — the card lists both; the file-level action is consistent.
O4: tmux shows only 20 of 106 reachable files with explicit +N aggregation; both reads understand the cap and one names it as a blocker for deeper flow.
O5: the edge labels are now explained ('distinct call count'); the median anchor legend removes the earlier 'ms' misread. The remaining LOW-confidence warning is honest and read aloud.
O6: no read found a bare cost number after the unit/anchor fix.
